newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fletcher Energy plans Brunei farm-out.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher Energy plans Brunei farm-out.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Energy said on Monday it had sought Brunei government approval to farm-out half of its interests in the Block A and CD Petroleum Mining Agreements in offshore Brunei to a large international energy resource company.
The company said the identity of the new joint venture party could not be disclosed until final approval was obtained.
Under the terms of the farm-out agreement, the new partner will acquire half of Fletcher Energy's 53.9 percent interest in Blocks A and CD. Fletcher Energy will continue as operator in both blocks.
The agreement does not relate to Block B, which contains the Maharaja Lela field, in which Fletcher Energy has a 35 percent stake.
"The introduction of a new partner will enable us to bring forward our exploration programme significantly while retaining exposure to any exploration rewards," Fletcher Energy said.

"Fletcher Challenge Energy has a strong commitment to developing a significant presence in Brunei. We believe these blocks, and the recently-announced Maharaja Lela field development in Block B, offer a range of exciting opportunities for us."

The company said that in exchange for gaining entry to the concessions, the new partner had agreed to fund the drilling of a number of exploration wells, including Perdana Deep-1, which was spudded on April 9.
It said the new partner had extensive experience in the region, having built an impressive exploration and development track record over a long period.
